result.topic_en: Riemann expands the phase θ − t log m around √(t/2π) = m+α to relate the last term of the zeta-function sum to a correction function f(σ), an early form of the Riemann–Siegel formula; in a side calculation he computes the coefficients a_{2k} (the Euler/secant numbers 1, −1, 5, −61, 1385, −50521, 2702765) by a binomial recurrence.
result.transcription:
$f(\sigma) = (-1)^{m+1}\frac{\cos(\sigma^2 2\pi + \frac{3}{8}\pi)}{2\sqrt[4]{\frac{t}{2\pi}}\,\cos 2\sigma\pi}$
$\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{t}{2\pi}} - m - \frac12$
$f(\sigma) + f(\sigma+1) = (-1)^m \frac{\cos((\sigma^2+\sigma+\frac12)2\pi + \frac38\pi)}{\sqrt[4]{\frac{t}{2\pi}}}$ [-$\cos(\sigma+\frac12)2\pi$-] $= (-1)^{m+1}\frac{\cos(\alpha\alpha 2\pi + \frac78\pi)}{\sqrt[4]{\frac{t}{2\pi}}}$

methods.what: Definition of the correction function in terms of σ = √(t/2π) − m − 1/2
Sum of two consecutive values of f reduces to a single cosine term
Taylor expansion of the phase θ − t log m with √(t/2π) = m+α
Approximation of the last sum term by a cosine in α (error O(1/√t))
Functional relation between the last term and the correction function
Binomial recurrence for the even coefficients a_{2k} (Euler/secant numbers) and their computation
